## Your goal

To become as strong at Go as you can: to keep improving, game after game, toward grandmaster-level play. The concrete target is to win consistently against the strongest opponent on the ladder, the 9d profile.

This session starts with no memory of the earlier ones: your conversation is not carried over. Your working directory does carry over: every file in it stays as you leave it. If AGENTS.md exists there, it is loaded into your context at the start of every session (its first 64 KiB); your other files are there to read with the file tools. What a later session knows of your earlier games is what you have left in these files.

## This game

A new game. You play Black, so you move first.

Rules: Chinese area scoring, with 7 points of komi for White; a level score is a draw. Simple ko: an immediate recapture is refused, and the board marks the ko point when there is one. Suicide is not allowed. An invalid move is refused with the rule it broke, and the turn stays with you. The game ends after two passes in a row or a resignation; a game that reaches 243 moves is scored where it stands. After two passes the engine scores the position as it stands and decides itself which stones are dead.

## Opponents

Your opponent is KataGo playing in the style of a human of the rank you choose. The ladder, weakest to strongest: 20k, 18k, 16k, 14k, 12k, 10k, 8k, 6k, 4k, 2k, 1d, 3d, 5d, 7d, 9d. You choose the rank with `choose_opponent(rank)` before the first move; it holds for the whole game, and you choose again in the next game.

## Tools

- Go: `choose_opponent(rank)`, `board()`, `play(move)` with a point or `pass`, and `resign()`.
- Files: `read_file(path)` and `list_files(path)` to read, and `apply_patch` to create, change and delete any file in your working directory.

You may write and run code. Use it only to inspect the current position and keep records — for example, to count stones or liberties, or check whether a move is legal. Do not build or use a Go engine, run Monte Carlo, search over sequences of future moves, or write a program that chooses, ranks or recommends moves.

## How this session ends

Play until the game is over. The final result comes back from your last Go call, followed by a closing note. Before you end the session after a game, write down in your working directory whatever will help the next session play better. The session ends when you end your turn.
I’ll review game 80, keep the opponent at 20k, and inspect each selected move’s resulting whole chain before playing. I’ll also track whether the opening leaves enough credible area to overcome komi.

Result: W+10 after 78 completed moves. Chinese area, komi 7, simple ko, no suicide. Captures Black 1 / White 14; no refused moves or ko. Seven wins, three draws, 70 losses overall; 77 scored games. ## Opening and allocation

Black E5; White C3/C7/E7/E3 spread upper and lower development. Black C5 separated the left footholds. F8 was separate with three liberties; Black G8 left two, then E8 joined F8/E7 with five. C8 had {B8,C9,D8}; upper White had five liberties. White44 D8 created actual private D7 and blocked the east route, leaving whole chain {A8,B8,D7,D9}. Black45 B8; White46 A8 joined, leaving {A9,D7,D9}; Black47 B9; White48 A9 left whole chain {D7,D9}, and Black B8/B9/C8 sole C9.

Actual Black49 E2 ignored the atari. White50 C9 captured3 SEPARATELY with {B9,C8,D9}. It was not joined diagonally to D8. Upper main gained new B8/B9/C8 liberties.

## Lower invasion: an error followed by a concrete recovery

Black49 E2 then51 D2; White52 C2 blocked the left route. Commentary predicted six whole-chain liberties; separate inspection showed FIVE {A3,B2,B3,C1,F1}. Corrected explicitly later. Black53 C1 was SEPARATE {B1,D1}, diagonal to D2.

White54 B1 was SEPARATE {A1,B2}, ataried C1 at D1. Black55 B2 left B1 soleA1. Extending A1 would have soleA2 and no checked immediate benefit, so abandoned B1. White56 A3 preserved the main boundary; Black57 A1 capturedB1. Crucially this capture REOPENED B1 for enemy B2 and C1; B2 was not still in the earlier two-liberty shape. An initial contemplated B3 was inspected, showed main only {A2,F1}, and rejected in favour of F1.

White58 F1 retained main {A2,B3,E1}; Black59 B3 left {A2,E1}, no established eyes. Filling A2 or E1 directly would leave the whole main chain in atari with no immediate capture. This was a serious original-group life emergency; winning the earlier area count did not guarantee survival. Review BEFORE B1/B2 and C2/C1, rather than relying on finding another recovery.

White60 D1 was a deliberately checked SEPARATE soleE1 move. Concrete benefit: Black E1 would join D2/E2, capture D1, and the WHOLE resulting three stones would have ONLY reopened D1; White D1 could capture3. This depended on all other surrounding points already being White. No generic permission to play sole-liberty stones.

Actual Black61 A2 instead joined A1/B2/B3. After that:

- Black A1/A2/B2/B3 soleB1.

White62 B1 captured FIVE simultaneously, SEPARATE {A1,B2,C1}, reopening A2/B3 for main and C1 for D1. This resolved the main-chain atari without filling E1. Black63 A2 re-entered; White64 E1 captured D2/E2 THROUGH main, joining D1 and F1, leaving {B2,B3,C1,D2,E2}.

Black67 B8, White68 C8 upstairs, Black69 E2 re-entered lower. White70 D2 captured1 THROUGH main, leaving distinct private {C1,E2}. Black71 F5 joined its outside chains. White72 A1 captured2, joining B1 with {A2,B2,C1}. Black passed73. White76 B2 joined that pair OUTSIDE, preserving three private eyes {A2,C1,E2}.

B1's first placement cost a stone, and the main group briefly reached soleE1. Survival depended on exact simultaneous captures and the opponent's replies. This win does not validate the earlier exposed lower framework or prove the D1 move forces a win against every reply.

Rules: Chinese area, komi 7, simple ko, no suicide. User's current instructions govern each game. Play through a result and save lessons and SGF before ending the session. Tools and analysis code may inspect the current board, count liberties and check legality; never build/use an engine, Monte Carlo, future-sequence search, or a program recommending/ranking moves.

Critical improvement: count DISTINCT liberties of ALL endangered friendly groups before each move. Joining groups does not guarantee safety. Check again after selecting a move, especially if it fills a friendly liberty. Game 1 lost six connected stones because the sole liberty J4 was overlooked. Use current-position-liberties.js as a counting aid, not as a move selector.

Before tenuki, identify opponent's immediate captures and cuts. Treat groups with one liberty as emergencies and two liberties as tactical concerns. Near the first line, assess escape routes before attaching: F8 in game 1 became trapped after F7/G8, and chasing along row 9 did not create an escape.

Do not describe groups as alive, connected safely, or enemy stones as dead without checking actual liberties and eye space. Distinguish observations from unverified strategic impressions.

Game 2 improvement: liberty counting alone is insufficient. Check actual eye space and an exit before enclosure. W34 D8 joined the upper group but left two liberties and no established eyes. Running F9/G9/H9 kept two liberties without escaping. Capturing C8 with C7 created only one eye; B45 J9 left 17 White stones with sole liberty C8, which White could not fill legally. An enemy stone in atari does not establish friendly life. Avoid filling interior space merely to connect.

Game 3 improvement: recognized the lost group's atari and finished by scoring. However, B31 C3 invaded without a concrete life/exit plan. D2/C2/B3 restricted it; C4/C5 extended toward enemy strength. B39 B4 kept three liberties without establishing eyes. A5/A6 repeated edge running; W44 A7 left seven stones with sole liberty A4. The main right chain had ten liberties, but controlling that side was insufficient. Assess rough area balance earlier, and reassess an invasion when replies remove its living space. Liberty counts describe danger; they do not establish a rescue.

Game 4 improvement: preserved D3 as an eye by connecting outside at C2, and built an upper boundary with substantial interior space. But W42 H3 entered the lower right without naming two usable eye regions. B43 H2 blocked the bottom route; B51 F6 joined the enclosing Black chains. Continuing with five liberties did not establish life. At the end, eight White stones had {G3,J1,J4,J5,J6}; G3/J1/J6 bordered Black stones and were not enclosed eyes, while adjacent J4/J5 formed one region. Identify two potential eye regions before an isolated entry, check which replies remove them, and reassess immediately when they disappear. Roughly 32 White area plus komi was insufficient if Black controlled the rest; assess balance before needing a late isolated group.

Game 5 improvement: outside connections D3/B2/G5 preserved a broad lower region and the main chain finished with ten liberties. But B29 C5 cut with only {B5,C6}, no eye, and an incorrect capture expectation. W30 B5 gained B6, leaving White {A5,B6}, while C5 was in atari at C6. Count newly exposed liberties when an enemy extends, not only old liberties filled. C6/C7 ran in successive ataris; C8 gained space, but D8/A8 closed it. Five cutting stones ended with {B9,C9} and no established eyes. The scorer returned W+8 without a dead-stone breakdown; no rescue was identified, not proven impossible. The lower framework was roughly 40 area against 41 plus komi before the risky cut. Assess area before partitioning the board; a smaller loss is not demonstrated winning strength.

Game 6 improvement: liberty counts exposed danger, but decisions still failed to preserve life. W18 G3 entered earlier, yet bottom/corner directions were not distinct secured eye regions. W30 H1 captured two Black stones; B31 G4 left White {F1,J1,J2}, with only one eye region J1/J2 and F1 as its sole external route. W32 F1, B33 E1 left eight stones with {J1,J2}. Identify distinct eye regions AND their required boundary points; check closure threats before answering interior invasions. Reassess after the first restrictive reply, not after enclosure. The connected left framework retained broad interior space but only roughly 24 area. The scorer gave B+26 without a dead-stone breakdown. Accurate counts must change choices earlier; no win demonstrated.

B41 F9 captured F8 and created a private eye. B43 J7 left White's four right stones in atari at J9; White could not fill J9 without suicide because Black retained F8. B45 J9 captured four, and B47 J8 joined the Black chains while preserving F8 and separate H6/H7/H8 eye space. The final main chain had 26 stones and those four empty points: only 30 area. Tactical success did not solve the early area deficit. B49 B7's lower route was blocked by B6, then C8/A7 restricted the top. A8/A9 were one potential region; C9 bordered White C8/D9 and was not an eye. B57 B5 blocked only one enemy connection route: W58 C6 joined B6 to the main chain, while B5 itself had two liberties and no eyes. B59 B4, W60 B3 repeated the narrow-edge failure; final liberties A4/A5/C4 did not establish two eyes. Reassess after the first restriction, check ALL enemy connection routes before cutting, and do not start a second group to rescue a failed entry without a concrete life plan. If legality is uncertain, inspect the resulting WHOLE friendly group; a joining move need not have immediate empty neighbors to be legal.

F2/E2 restricted the bottom early; D2/D1 completed its enclosure. Before F3, the lower chain had {C2,C4,D3,F3}; only C4 was private, while the others bordered connected Black chains.
